findings.finding: Infrastructure and software peers that reported in the last week beat and were sold hard on their outlooks. F5 beat revenue ($917.4m vs $884.0m expected) but guided FY27 growth to 8-9% against 11%, with gross margin pressured by higher component costs, and fell 20.4% on 2026-10-28. Twilio beat by 3% and fell 15.2%. The market is punishing beat-and-soft-guide this week, and Fastly's next-quarter guide is the line it trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-05): revenue beat by about $10m against the guide midpoint and the FY guide was raised, yet the stock fell 12.87%. Q1 2026 (2026-05-06): better-than-expected results, -38.23% on core network-services deceleration (https://www.metatrader.com/fr/news/1640036-fastly-stock-plunges-42-after-q1-earnings-time-to-stay-cautious).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a regime read rather than a company fact, and FSLY's own 5-day -22% already absorbed part of the sector selloff. If the market believed Fastly would escape it, the put skew would not be +4.5 and the stock would not sit at the low end of its 20-day range. The size is small because most of this sits in the price and the skew.
findings.independence: StockStory's Fastly preview (2026-11-03) reports the F5 -20.4% and Twilio -15.2% reactions independently (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/fsly/news/earnings/fastly-fsly-q3-earnings-what-to-expect). It shares the F5 component-cost point with the memory finding below; that point is counted only there.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide of $732-746m, less Q1 $173.0m, Q2 $183.3m and the Q3 guide of $184-190m, implies Q4 2026 revenue of about $185.7-205.7m (midpoint $195.7m). Against Q4 2025's $172.6m that is about +13% at the midpoint, down from 18% guided for Q3 and 23% reported in Q2. On the Q2 call management also flagged a harder Q4 net-retention comparison. Unless the FY guide is raised again, the forward guide reads as a deceleration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY guide was raised in Q1 (to $710-725m) and in Q2 (to $732-746m). The raise in Q2 still met -12.9%, and the deceleration in Q1 network services met -38.2%. The Q4 2025 print with a strong 2026 guide was +72.3% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public, but previews quote 18.7% Q3 growth and no Q4 figure (StockStory 2026-11-03). Consensus probably already carries a raise. The size is small because Fastly has raised every quarter this year, so the real question is the size of the raise against a bar nobody publishes.
findings.independence: Q1 revenue is $173.0m per the Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001517413/000151741326000129/ex991-fslypressrelease33126.htm). Q4 2025 is $172.61m (https://finviz.com/news/312183/fastly-inc-fsly-reports-fourth-quarter-revenue-of-17261-million-ahead-of-consensus). The harder Q4 NRR comparison is from the Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/12/fastly-fsly-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/).

findings.finding: Fastly has beaten the midpoint of its own revenue guide in each recent quarter: Q2 came in at $183.3m against a $170-176m guide, $10m above the midpoint. Benzinga/Zacks history shows revenue surprises of +0.7% to +7% over the last four quarters. Q3 consensus of about $187.6m sits at the guide midpoint, so another beat is likely. The CFO said under half of the Q2 upside was episodic (World Cup, with 75% of games in Q2) and that the Q3 guide is otherwise normal Q2-to-Q3 seasonality.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats were sold in Q1 2026 (-38.2%) and Q2 2026 (-12.9%), and bought in Q4 2025 (+72.3%), Q3 2025 (+35.9%) and Q2 2025 (+14.4%) (baseline). The reported-quarter beat has not been the deciding line in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: A habitual beat is mostly priced: the whisper of about $190.8m already sits near the top of the guide. What is not priced is the size. If the market expected a repeat of Q2's 5-6% upside, the whisper would be about $197m rather than $190.8m.
findings.independence: Beat history from the Q3 preview search (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FSLY/earnings). The whisper is from Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/x/FSLY).

findings.finding: Remaining performance obligations fell sequentially from $369m at Q1 2026 to $341m at Q2 2026, although they were still up 38% y/y. Current RPO was about $269m (79%), up 44%. The CFO tied RPO to upfront commitments at onboarding. A second sequential decline in the Q3 10-Q or release would be a visible negative data point on forward commitments.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean history of RPO alone moving the stock. In Q2 it fell q/q and the stock fell 12.9%, but that move was attributed to growth outside the top 10 (12%) and to episodic upside.
findings.why_not_priced: Most write-ups quote the +38% y/y RPO figure rather than the q/q decline. If the q/q decline had registered, previews would mention it, and none found does. The size is small because it is one quarter of a lumpy metric.
findings.independence: The Q2 figure of $341m is in the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001517413/000151741326000212/ex991-fslypressrelease63026.htm). This shares that document with the Q4 guide finding but is a different line.

findings.finding: Concentration risk is rising. The top 10 customers were 37% of Q2 revenue, up from 31% a year earlier, and grew 48% against 12% for everyone else. One group under common control was 11% of revenue. The Q1 10-Q names TikTok as one of the largest customers and says Fastly does not know how the U.S. restructuring will affect traffic. Any disclosure in Q3 of a top-customer traffic shift would be a large negative. No dated report of such a shift was found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 call disclosed that customers outside the top 10 grew only 12%, and the stock fell 12.9%. The precedent for a top-customer traffic move is ByteDance removing most TikTok traffic in Q3 2020 (https://www.gizchina.com/2020/10/29/bytedance-expunged-most-of-tiktok-traffic-from-fastly/). The size of that reaction is not sourced here.
findings.source_date: 2026-05 (Q1 2026 10-Q for the period ended 2026-03-31; exact filing day not read)
findings.why_not_priced: The risk is known, and the realised outcome (whether the top-10 share holds at 37-39%, as the CFO guided) is unseen. Net of the rest of the company: the 63% outside the top 10 grows about 12% and security grows about 43%, so a top-customer wobble would have to be large to miss the guide. That is why this is sized small, with a wide downside tail.
findings.independence: The top-10 figures and the 11% common-control group are from the Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/12/fastly-fsly-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). This is a different document from the 10-Q.

findings.finding: Memory-cost inflation is a gross-margin and capex risk. TrendForce forecast Q3 2026 server DRAM contract prices up 13-18% q/q, after 53-58% in Q2, with buyers without long-term agreements bearing most of it. Fastly guided capex to 10-12% of revenue (about 5% in 2025), said it is 'closely monitoring supply chain dynamics particularly regarding memory components', and guided gross margin to 65% ±50bp. F5 guided its FY27 gross margin lower on higher component costs on 2026-10-28.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 gross margin was a record 65.8%, 180bp above the guide, and the stock still fell 12.9%. In April 2026 a Craig-Hallum downgrade citing capex and memory costs coincided with a -14% day (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/why-fastly-stock-plunged-14-tuesday).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro-to-company proxy that the company has flagged but not quantified. If it were priced, the FY FCF guide of $40-50m would already be cut in consensus, and no source shows that. The size is small because it is a proxy and the cost runs mostly through depreciation, so it reaches COGS with a lag.
findings.independence: F5's component-cost margin guide (https://www.trefis.com/stock/ffiv/articles/621359/what-just-happened-to-ffiv-stock/2026-10-29) is a direct counterparty-class confirmation. Fastly's own memory language is on the Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/12/fastly-fsly-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/).

The largest single drop was -12.3% on 2026-10-30, a sector-wide AI-capex selloff after Amazon and Intel reported, not Fastly news. Short interest is 13.8% of float. findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is priced by definition. What is not visible is whether it over-discounted a company that has not spoken since August. If it had been read as Fastly-specific, the drop would have come with a Fastly news item, and the only one found is the macro selloff. Sized small: the cause is macro and the skew still pays downside.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly negative, which agrees with the +4.5 put skew and the -22% 5-day run-up. They are therefore mostly in the price, which is why p_up sits only 4 points below 50. The 13.8% short interest and the macro, rather than company-specific, cause of the drawdown are the counterweight.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the reported-quarter beat finding went from +1.5 to +0.8, because FSLY sold its last two beats (-38.2%, -12.9%).

Lesson 7 (positioning): the peer-sell-off negative agrees with the +4.5 downside skew and the -22% 5-day tape, so it was shrunk from -1.5 to -1.0. Short interest (13.8% of float, 2.6 days) was looked up before filing any negative.
Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): the positioning/de-rating positive went from +2.0 to +1.0. The drawdown has a named macro cause, so it is kept, but it is still largely priced.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the bar was sourced to the company guide because the two revenue consensus sources disagree ($187.6m vs $190.8m) and EPS consensus is disputed. The Q4 implied-guide finding went from -1.0 to -0.8, because the company raised its FY guide in both prior quarters.
Lessons 5 and 9 (proxy; segment net of the rest): the memory-proxy and customer-concentration findings were left at -0.5, already sized small and net of the 63% of revenue outside the top 10.
p_up moved from 48 to 46 and impact_sum from -0.6 to -1.6. Shrinking the positives (the beat and the de-rating) more than the negatives tipped the net lean down. abs_move was left at 20.
